findings.reason: the plan should either extend this assembler for tree branches or add it to §5's deletion list, so a reviewer of §4 knows whether the branch read is reused or supersedes separatrix_branches.
findings.text: the plan's reuse search (scout c94c95408) records nova's "two critical-point polish kernels" and "no join tree" but does not record assemble_separatrix_branches, which already splits a level set at its saddle into one closed axis lobe and open legs — the exact branch structure §4 defines as "the other branches that join at the primary X-point"; §4 therefore proposes new private-region machinery over an existing assembler

findings.reason: naming the owner forces §4 to state whether the tree replaces private_flux_mask or layers over it, which decides whether the mask and its shadow test are deleted in §5.
findings.text: private_flux_mask already computes the private-flux region from the flux map, and topology_margin's docstring reads its "private-flux shadow" as the exclusion of a wall extremum; §4's "Private regions ... a wall contact inside a private region can never be a limiter" restates this concept without citing the existing mask or its consumer

findings.reason: a design review of a "one authority" plan can only judge its depth if the plan names the module that owns §3/§4 and which of these three surfaces is its public interface; without that, §3 and §4 may accrete as wrappers over the landed receipt rather than into it.
findings.text: the plan says "one module that is the sole source of every topology verdict" and §1 promises "one result type (a dataclass returned by the read)", but build_contour_tree returns a device ContourTreeArrays, the §1-contract dataclass ContourTreeResult is produced by no function in the module, and dd_emittable_nodes adds a third host-selection surface; the substantial §3 polish and §4 selection/margin behaviour is given no module or interface in the plan text

findings.reason: naming the owner forces §5 to declare whether the branch assembler is retired or re-based on the tree, without which the "sole source of every topology verdict" claim is contradicted by a live parallel branch reader.
findings.text: assemble_separatrix_branches is the owner of "one closed axis branch and fixed slots of saddle-ended legs" and is consumed in production by nova/media/poloidal.py:365 draw_separatrix_branches; §4's branch/private-region read reasons over the same structure off the tree, yet §5's deletion list names only _axis_component_before_level, the sightline test, the raster hex partition and the census contact polish — not this file

findings.reason: the plan's sole-authority claim is only testable once §5 names private_flux_mask and the topology.py private-shadow reads as replaced by §4's tree region, and the done-when "a search of the touched modules finds no normalised-flux value feeding a classification" should extend to a search for a second private-region read.
findings.text: private_flux_mask is the owner of the private-flux region and is fed by topology.py's private_wall_node_read/x_point_height_limits private-shadow path (topology.py:52,69); §4 re-derives the private region, and §5's deletion list writes "the axis, X-point and wall-anchor reads in topology.py" without naming the private-shadow read, so two private-region implementations survive a plan whose stated purpose is a sole authority

findings.reason: the plan's §5 must enumerate this owner or the "no module references the deleted functions" done-when is false by construction while a shadowed-contact read remains live.
findings.text: private_wall_node_read and x_point_height_limits (topology.py:52) are the current private-shadow wall reader that §4's margin definition ("σψ over the wall vertices that do not lie in a private region") replaces, and §5 does not name them for deletion

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the plan promises one authority module with one result type but names no interface for §3's polished geometry or §4's class/margin, and the landed read exposes three host surfaces (ContourTreeArrays, ContourTreeResult, dd_emittable_nodes) rather than the single dataclass §1 describes.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's private-region branch structure duplicates an existing owner, nova/equilibrium/separatrix_branches.py::assemble_separatrix_branches, which §5's deletion list never names.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §4's private-region and primary-branch read proposes new machinery although nova/equilibrium/separatrix_branches.py::assemble_separatrix_branches and nova/equilibrium/flux_surface_connectivity.py::private_flux_mask already assemble the axis branch plus saddle-ended legs and the private-flux region, and the plan's reuse map cites neither.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §5 cuts consumers over to the tree and deletes the raster reads; no thin wrapper over the tree is proposed.
